files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller checklist

Owner: F. Boudreau. Complete these steps in sequence and leave support for each conclusion.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; note that in some months every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm that June prepaid amortization agrees to the prepaid schedule and underlying contracts. Check the GL first to avoid a duplicate, and if the entry is missing, record June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL to ensure it has not already been recorded.
5. Compare the June vendor-bill documents with the GL expense coding. Verify that each bill is in the correct expense account and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Once items 1-5 are posted, prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Foxglove Market Inc. began in 2018 when two former specialty-store buyers started assembling practical, design-conscious home and desk goods for customers who wanted a more personal alternative to large online marketplaces. The founders initially packed orders around a shared worktable, learning quickly which products traveled well, photographed honestly, and earned repeat purchases.

Today, the company operates as a small ecommerce merchant focused on stationery, organization tools, giftable household accessories, and seasonal collections from independent makers. Its assortment is deliberately edited rather than enormous. Product pages emphasize clear dimensions, materials, care notes, and straightforward photography so customers know what will arrive.

The team has the friendly, improvised rhythm common to a small retailer. Merchandising and marketing trade ideas constantly; customer support passes recurring questions back to the product team; and operations keeps a close eye on packaging, carrier handoffs, and inventory accuracy. Everyone helps during busy campaign periods, even if that means proofreading an email or folding packing inserts.

Foxglove Market Inc. is currently refining its brand presentation, improving fulfillment routines, and strengthening relationships with retail and business customers. Management remains focused on dependable service, useful products, and measured growth while the accounting team works to make reporting and month-end processes more consistent.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Give Foxglove Market Inc. a warmer, more consistent brand voice across the storefront, email, social channels, and package inserts. The refresh should feel useful and human rather than overly polished.

## Priorities

- Update core messaging and visual guidelines, then apply them first to high-traffic product and collection pages.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, using practical themes such as workspace organization, thoughtful gifting, and care for everyday goods.
- Test a partner co-marketing pilot with a complementary independent brand. Favor shared editorial content and audience fit over broad reach.
- Build campaign briefs around seasonal customer needs, with merchandising, inventory, and customer support represented before launch.
- Repurpose webinar questions into short guides, email features, and social posts.

## Measurement

Track qualified site visits, email engagement, repeat purchasing, webinar participation, partner-referred traffic, and customer-service themes. Review results after each campaign and record what should be repeated, revised, or dropped.

## Open items

Final channel mix and production scope remain pending the Q2 close. Confirm team capacity before committing to creative work, and keep contingency concepts ready for products with uncertain availability.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes for the handoff

F. Boudreau — a few things I learned the hard way:

- The bank's own service fees and charges usually show up near the end of the statement. They are generally not in the books beforehand, so we record them during the close.
- I was moving too fast in June, and the expense coding on one or two vendor bills may be wrong. Treat the underlying documents in `bills/` as authoritative and reclass the GL where needed.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. The one-off items that arrived in June were never planned, and they are the reason the larger variances appear.
- Payroll timing is unusual this month: the second June run pays in early July. Check the payroll register and handle the accrual from there.
